problems.title: A repeating decimal as a fraction
problems.question: Calculate 1/9−0.(7)+1/3.
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: $0.\overline7=7/9$.

problems.title: Last digit of a difference of powers
problems.question: Find the last digit of 2027^2027−2023^2022.
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: Last digits repeat in cycles of four: powers of 7 give 7,9,3,1; powers of 3 give 3,9,7,1.
steps: 2027 leaves remainder 3 on division by 4, so the first power ends in 3. The exponent 2022 leaves remainder 2, so the second ends in 9.
Subtract modulo 10: 3−9≡4.

problems.title: Distinct prime divisors
problems.question: How many prime divisors does 630 have?
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: $630=2\cdot3^2\cdot5\cdot7$.
steps: The distinct prime divisors are 2,3,5,7, giving four. Repeated prime factors do not add new divisors to this list.

problems.title: Midpoints on a line in two configurations
problems.question: A,B,C lie on a line with AB=7,BC=9. Which listed distance between midpoints of AB and BC is possible?
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: With B at 0, the midpoint coordinates are half the coordinates of A and C.
steps: If A and C lie on the same side of B, the midpoint distance is (9−7)/2=1. If they lie on opposite sides, it is (9+7)/2=8.
Only 1 is among the printed choices.
problems.answer: 1 cm among the choices; all possible distances are 1 and 8 cm.

problems.title: Three lines sharing marked intersections
problems.question: Three distinct lines contain 3,4,5 marked points respectively. What is the least total number of distinct marked points?
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: Two distinct lines can share at most one point.
steps: Start with the total count 3+4+5=12. To reduce the distinct count most, use three nonparallel, nonconcurrent lines and mark all three pairwise intersections. Each intersection is counted twice, saving 3.
Add the other required points away from the intersections. This realizes 12−3=9. Three concurrent lines would save only 2.

problems.title: Apply a custom operation twice
problems.question: If a⋈b=3a+b², calculate (5⋈2)⋈3.
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: Use the defining rule for the inner operation first.

problems.title: Count divisors after factoring 24
problems.question: How many positive divisors does a=24·7²·11²·13 have?
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: $24=2^3\cdot3$; if $N=\prod p_i^{e_i}$ then divisor count $=\prod(e_i+1)$.
steps: The prime exponents are 3,1,2,2,1. Each divisor independently chooses an exponent from 0 to the corresponding maximum.
The count is 4×2×3×3×2=144.

problems.title: Smallest product of consecutive even positive integers
problems.question: What is the least product of five consecutive positive even integers?
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: The smallest five are 2,4,6,8,10; increasing any starting value increases every factor.

problems.title: Supplementary angles in a ratio
problems.question: Two adjacent supplementary angles satisfy (2/7)A=(2/5)B. Find |A−B|.
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
steps: The angle ratio is A:B=7:5. Twelve equal parts total 180°, so each is 15°. The angles are 105°,75° and their difference is 30°.

problems.title: Three interior angles at parallel lines
problems.question: A pair of alternate interior angles plus one other interior angle total 220°. Find the largest of the eight angles.
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: Alternate interior angles are equal; adjacent interior angle sizes sum to 180°.
steps: Write the equal pair as x,x and the other size as 180°−x. The sum is 180°+x=220°, so x=40°.
The other angle size is 140°, the larger.

problems.title: Union with an intersection
problems.question: A={1,3,5,6,7}, B={3,5,7,8,9}, C={1,2,3,5,9,11}. Find |A∪(B∩C)|.
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: Intersection keeps common elements; union keeps each element once.
steps: B∩C={3,5,9}. Adding these to A gives {1,3,5,6,7,9}, containing six elements.

problems.title: Subsets of a multiples set
problems.question: A contains all two-digit positive multiples of 22. How many subsets does A have?
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: An n-element set has $2^n$ subsets.
steps: A={22,44,66,88} has four elements, so it has 2⁴=16 subsets, including the empty set.

problems.title: A natural-number reciprocal equation
problems.question: Positive integers a,b satisfy 1/a+2/b=1. Find the possible values of a+b.
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
steps: a=1 is impossible. For b to be integral, a−1 must be a positive divisor of 2. Thus a=2,b=4 or a=3,b=3.
Both pairs have sum 6.

problems.title: Clock hands at 13:42
problems.question: Find the smaller angle between clock hands at 13:42.
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: Minute angle $=6m$; hour angle $=30h+m/2$, with h counted modulo 12.
steps: At 1:42 the minute hand is at 252° and hour hand at 30°+21°=51°. Their difference is 201°.
The smaller angle is 360°−201°=159°.

problems.title: A point inside a subsegment
problems.question: K lies on AB, AK=10,KB=20. N lies on KB and 5NA=4(NK+NB). Find NK.
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: $NK+NB=KB=20$ and $NA=AK+KN$.
steps: 5NA=80, so NA=16. Subtract AK=10 to get NK=6. This lies between 0 and 20 as required.

problems.title: Reduce each factor modulo seven
problems.question: Find the remainder of 17·18·19·23·37 on division by 7.
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: Products can be reduced factor by factor modulo 7.
steps: The remainders are 3,4,5,2,2. Their product is 240, which is 2 modulo 7.

problems.title: Five statements involving possible increases and divisibility
problems.question: Count the true statements: (1) a positive fraction can increase after numerator +2 and denominator −4; (2) after numerator +1 and denominator +12; (3) three consecutive primes can have even product; (4) three consecutive positive integers have even product; (5) four consecutive positive integers have product divisible by 6.
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: A possibility needs one example; a universal claim needs an argument for every case.
steps: (1) 1/5 becomes 3/1, an increase. (2) 1/20 becomes 2/32=1/16, also an increase.
(3) Consecutive primes 2,3,5 have even product. (4) Any three consecutive integers include an even integer. (5) Any four include both an even integer and a multiple of 3.
All five statements are true.

problems.title: Subtract a containing set
problems.question: A is the set of divisors of 64 and B of divisors of 560. How many elements are in (A∩B)∖B?
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: $A\cap B\subseteq B$.
steps: Every element of the intersection already belongs to B. Removing B therefore removes every element.

problems.title: Maximum regions from five lines
problems.question: What is the maximum number of regions formed by five lines in a plane?
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: The nth new line adds at most n regions; $R_n=1+n(n+1)/2$.
steps: Choose no parallel pairs and no triple intersections. Then the five lines add 1,2,3,4,5 regions to the original one. Total=1+15=16.

problems.title: Bisectors of angles made by two lines
problems.question: What can the angle between bisector rays of any two different angles formed by intersecting lines be?
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: Bisectors of adjacent supplementary angles are perpendicular; bisectors of opposite angles are opposite rays.
steps: For adjacent angles, half their sum is 180°/2=90°. For vertically opposite angles, the bisector rays point in opposite directions and form 180°.

problems.title: Sports participation in a class
problems.question: One third of a class are boys. One fifth of the boys and one sixth of the girls play sports; eight students total play sports. Find the digit sum of class size n.
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: Sports count $=n/15+(2n/3)/6=8n/45$.
steps: Set 8n/45=8 to obtain n=45. This gives 15 boys and 30 girls, of whom 3 and 5 play sports. The digit sum is 4+5=9.

problems.title: Compare an absolute-value sum at six candidates
problems.question: At which listed x∈{−7,−4,−1,2,4,6} is |x+10|+|x+8|+|x+7|+|x−4|+|x−5|+|x−10| largest?
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: For each candidate add its distances to −10,−8,−7,4,5,10.
steps: In the given order the sums are 44,44,44,44,44,50. The only largest value is 50 at x=6.

problems.title: Find a possible cancellation factor
problems.question: Which listed integer can be a common divisor of 3n+1 and 19n+14 for positive integer n?
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: Any common divisor divides $19(3n+1)-3(19n+14)=-23$.
steps: A nontrivial common divisor must be 23. It is attainable: for n=15 the fraction is 46/299=(2×23)/(13×23).

problems.title: A distance that determines the inner points
problems.question: Four distinct collinear points satisfy AD=24,BC=12. Which listed CD∈{2,4,6,8,12,36} uniquely identifies the two points between the outer two?
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: Put A=0,D=24; then $C=24\pm d$ and $B=C\pm12$.
steps: For d=12, C can be 12 or 36. C=12 forces B=0 or 24, violating distinctness. C=36 permits B=48 (B=24 is invalid). Thus the order is A,D,C,B, so D and C are the inner points.
For each d=2,4,6,8, there are at least two different inner pairs: C=24−d,B=12−d gives inner B,C; C=24+d,B=36+d gives inner D,C.
For d=36, C=60 with B=48 gives inner D,B, while B=72 gives inner D,C. Therefore only d=12 gives a fixed inner pair.
problems.answer: CD=12; the inner points are C and D.

problems.title: A bisector between parallel lines
problems.question: AB∥DM, CB∥MN; CM bisects BCD, ABC=32°,CDM=108°. Find CMN in the given diagram.
problems.idea: Turn the information into simple arithmetic or a geometric relation, then check the result.
formulas: Corresponding angles at parallel lines match; a bisector halves an angle.
steps: Take the parallels as horizontal. Ray CB makes 32° above the rightward direction. Since CDM=108°, ray CD makes 72° below it.
Thus BCD=32°+72°=104°. Ray CM is halfway between those directions, 20° below horizontal. Its reverse MC is at 160°, while MN is at 32°.
The angle CMN is 160°−32°=128°.
